pages.hook: In Seattle, a coffee order is a small list of choices: drink, size, milk and temperature. Learn the list and you can order your way anywhere in the USA.

mythfact.s: The coffee company Starbucks began in Seattle.
mythfact.why: Starbucks opened its first shop in Seattle in 1971.

mythfact.s: In the USA, people only drink hot coffee.
mythfact.why: Iced coffee and iced lattes are very common, even in winter.

mythfact.s: Oat milk is made from oats.
mythfact.why: It is a plant-based milk, a popular choice instead of cow’s milk.

mythfact.s: A barista chooses your size for you.
mythfact.why: You choose: small, medium or large. The barista asks you.

mythfact.s: The Great British Bake Off is filmed in a big tent.
mythfact.why: The bakers work in a large tent in the countryside.

decode.q: How much is a medium latte with oat milk?

lines: Please wait here for your name.

decode.q: What should you do after you order?

compare.br: In Brazil, a small hot cafezinho is the normal coffee, and people often drink it standing at the counter.
compare.us: In the USA, coffee has many choices: size, milk, hot or iced. The barista asks and you answer one by one.
compare.tip: Answer each question with one short word: Medium. Oat milk. Hot.
compare.ask: How do you like your coffee? Say it in English.

quiz.q: The barista asks: “Hot or iced?” You want a cold drink. You say…
quiz.why: Answer with one word and please.
A latte is espresso with a lot of milk.

Reading quest — Coffee first, cake later · part 1
text: My friend Joy lives in **Seattle**. She loves coffee. Every morning she goes to a small café near her house. Today I went with her, and I learned a lot.

At the counter, the barista smiled and said, “**What can I get started for you?**” Joy said, “A latte, please.” “**What size?**” “Medium. **With oat milk.**” “**Hot or iced?**” “Hot, please.” Her order was clear, short and polite.

Then the barista asked, “**Anything to eat?**” Joy chose a **blueberry muffin**. I laughed because it looked like a small cake. Joy said, “I need my **caffeine fix**!” The barista answered, “Have a great day!”

pages.title: Reading quest — Coffee first, cake later · part 2
text: At home, we watched The Great British Bake Off. It is a baking show from 2010. Bakers make cakes and bread in a big tent. They follow a recipe, watch the timer and check the oven. “The oven is hot! Time’s up!” the hosts say.
I want to bake a cake, too. I can make the cake, and Joy can make the coffee. We can eat together. For me, coffee is more fun with a friend and something sweet.

pages.think: How do you like your coffee or tea? Say your order in English.

qs.q: Mei says: “Hi! What can I get started for you?” — what is the natural reply?
Mei says: “What size? Small, medium or large?” — what is the natural reply?
opts: Medium size is good for me.

qs.q: Mei says: “Hot or iced?” — what is the natural reply?
Mei says: “Anything to eat?” — what is the natural reply?

pages.title: Choose your reply · 1/2
pages.story: You are in a café in Seattle. Mei is the barista. Order your latte your way.

turns.npc: Hi! What can I get started for you?

opts.fb: Use A latte, please or I’d like…
It does not answer the question.

turns.npc: What size? Small, medium or large?

opts.en: Medium size is good for me.
opts.pt: Tamanho médio é bom para mim.

opts.fb: Answer the size, then add the milk.
It is about size, not time.

opts.fb: Wrong tense and not an order.
Use it after Thank you, not here.

pages.title: Sound lab · listen & choose

speed.q: Complete a fala: “I need my ____.” (Preciso da minha dose de cafeína.)
Complete a fala: “Same! ____.” (Eu também! Sou um zumbi sem café.)
speed.why: “I'm dead without it” = Sou um zumbi sem isso

opts: Que tamanho? Pequeno, médio ou grande?
Pode mandar mensagem pra Mia também?
São dez dólares. Quer um capacete?

dict.say: Hi! What can I get started for you?

errors.why: In English the adjective goes before the noun: a hot latte.
Say the size, then please.
The first noun describes the second: oat milk.
Use I’d like or I want. Not “am wanting”.
